category: Structural material models I: linear/nonlinear elastic, hyperelastic, viscoelastic, damping and special materials
description: Material models of the Solid Mechanics family (Structural Mechanics and Nonlinear Structural Materials Modules): elasticity input options, hyperelastic strain energy models, Mullins effect, fibers, viscoelastic rheologies and shift functions, damping models, shape memory alloys and other constitutive nodes. Feature type strings and property-group names were verified against COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models.

tools.name: Isotropic Elasticity Input Pairs (Linear Elastic Material)
tools.description: For an isotropic Linear Elastic Material the elastic constants can be entered as any of five equivalent pairs: Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio, Young's modulus and shear modulus, bulk and shear modulus, Lame parameters, or pressure- and shear-wave speeds. COMSOL converts between them internally, so choose the pair that matches your test data (wave speeds for ultrasonics, K-G for nearly incompressible solids). Density is only needed for dynamics, gravity/rotating-frame loads and mass properties.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Linear Elastic Material section > Material symmetry = Isotropic, Specify = <pair>. Java: physics("solid").feature("lemm1").set("IsotropicOption", "Enu" | "KG" | "Lame" | "CpCs"); matching material property groups: Enu, EG, KG, Lame, CpCs.

parameters.name: IsotropicOption
parameters.description: Enu (E, nu), EG-type (E, G), KG (bulk K, shear G), Lame (lambda, mu), CpCs (cp, cs).

parameters.name: E, nu / K, G / lambLame, muLame / cp, cs
parameters.description: Property names in the corresponding material property group; each can be From material or User defined.

parameters.name: rho
parameters.description: Density, From material by default; needed for inertia, gravity and wave-speed input.

tools.notes: Cp/Cs input is used, for example, in the Elastic Waves, Time Explicit models (angle_beam_ndt). In plane stress the actual longitudinal wave speed is lower than the entered cp. Very large K/G ratios call for the Mixed Formulation.

tools.name: Orthotropic and Transversely Isotropic (Linear Elastic Material)
tools.description: Orthotropic material symmetry defines three Young's moduli, three Poisson's ratios and three shear moduli along the axes of the selected coordinate system; the Transversely isotropic option reduces this to five constants with the first local axis as the special direction. It is the standard choice for wood, unidirectional composite plies, rolled metals and single-crystal-like textures. Material data can be ordered in Standard or Voigt notation.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Material symmetry = Orthotropic (check Transversely isotropic if needed); select a local Coordinate system on the node. Java: feature("lemm1").set("SolidModel", "Orthotropic"); material property groups Orthotropic (Evector, nuvector, Gvector), OrthotropicVoGrp or TransverseIsotropic (Evect, nuvect, Gvect1).

parameters.name: SolidModel
parameters.description: Isotropic | Orthotropic | Anisotropic (Crystal in the GUI for Solid Mechanics).

parameters.name: Evector, nuvector, Gvector
parameters.description: E1..E3, nu12/nu23/nu13 and G12/G23/G13 in the local system.

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: Orthonormal system in the material frame that defines the principal axes (Rotated, Curvilinear, Base Vector system).

tools.notes: Check which Poisson's ratio convention (nu_ij vs nu_ji) the data source uses. Orthotropic and anisotropic options require the Structural Mechanics, MEMS or Composite Materials Module. Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Plasticity/orthotropic_container.

tools.name: Anisotropic and Crystal Symmetry (Linear Elastic Material)
tools.description: Anisotropic symmetry takes a full symmetric 6x6 elasticity matrix D (or compliance matrix) in Standard or Voigt ordering, for materials with no symmetry planes, such as homogenized unit cells or rotated crystals. Crystal symmetry (Solid Mechanics only) needs just the independent constants of the crystal system: Cubic (3), Hexagonal (5), Trigonal (6 or 7), Tetragonal (6 or 7) or Orthorhombic (9).
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Material symmetry = Anisotropic or Crystal. Java: feature("lemm1").set("SolidModel", "Anisotropic"); feature("lemm1").set("AnisotropicOption", "AnisotropicStd" | "AnisotropicVo"); material groups Anisotropic (D) or AnisotropicVoGrp (DVo).

parameters.name: AnisotropicOption
parameters.description: AnisotropicStd (xx, yy, zz, xy, yz, xz ordering) or AnisotropicVo (Voigt: xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy).

parameters.name: D / DVo
parameters.description: Upper triangle of the 6x6 elasticity matrix (or compliance matrix when that option is chosen).

parameters.name: Crystal system
parameters.description: Cubic, Hexagonal, Trigonal, Tetragonal, Orthorhombic (GUI option for the Crystal symmetry).

tools.notes: In 1D and 1D axisymmetric models the matrix is interpreted as isotropic/orthotropic only. Loss factors for anisotropic damping use eta_D / eta_DVo in the same groups. Application Library: Structural_Mechanics_Module/Material_Models/isotropic_anisotropic_sample.

tools.name: Mixed Formulation (Solid Mechanics Material Models)
tools.description: For nearly incompressible materials (Poisson's ratio close to 0.5, rubber, plastic flow at large strain) a pure displacement formulation locks. The Use mixed formulation setting adds an extra dependent variable for the pressure (Pressure formulation) or the volumetric strain (Strain formulation) to remove volumetric locking; an Implicit formulation is available with plane stress. It is available on Linear Elastic, Nonlinear Elastic and Hyperelastic Material nodes.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material (or Hyperelastic/Nonlinear Elastic) > Mixed Formulation > Use mixed formulation = None | Pressure formulation | Strain formulation. Java: feature("lemm1").set("MixedFormulation", "pFormulation").

parameters.name: MixedFormulation
parameters.description: none | pFormulation (pressure) | strain formulation; not available in Solid Mechanics, Explicit Dynamics.

parameters.name: Auxiliary pressure discretization
parameters.description: Automatic, Discontinuous Lagrange, Continuous, Linear or Constant (Advanced Physics Options).

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("solid").feature("lemm1").set("MixedFormulation", "pFormulation");
// hyperelastic: choosing Compressibility = Nearly incompressible selects the pressure formulation automatically
tools.notes: A mixed formulation makes the system a saddle-point problem; use a direct solver or the suggested iterative settings. Reduced integration with hourglass stabilization is an alternative way to mitigate locking.

tools.name: Geometric Nonlinearity and Strain Decomposition (Solid Mechanics Material Models)
tools.description: Every material node has a Geometric Nonlinearity section that controls the kinematics: From study step (large strain when Include geometric nonlinearity is checked), Total Lagrangian (forces large deformation in all steps) or Geometrically linear. When inelastic strains are present the Strain decomposition can be Automatic, Additive, Logarithmic (additive Hencky) or Multiplicative, which determines how elastic and inelastic parts (plastic, thermal, creep) are separated.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material node> > Geometric Nonlinearity > Formulation / Strain decomposition. Java: feature("lemm1").set("geometricNonlinearity", "fromStudyStep" | "totalLagrangian" | "linear"); feature("lemm1").set("strainDecomposition", "automatic" | "additiveHencky" | "multiplicative").

parameters.name: geometricNonlinearity
parameters.description: fromStudyStep, totalLagrangian or linear (geometrically linear, small strain).

parameters.name: strainDecomposition
parameters.description: automatic, additive, additiveHencky (logarithmic) or multiplicative.

parameters.name: henckyApproximation
parameters.description: builtIn or Pade approximation of the logarithmic strain.

tools.notes: Hyperelastic materials are always geometrically nonlinear. Mixing geometrically linear and nonlinear materials in one component is possible but the study-step checkbox is then forced on. See also the existing entry Include Geometric Nonlinearity.

tools.name: Reduced Integration and Hourglass Stabilization (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: The Quadrature Settings section of the material nodes can switch to reduced integration, which is faster and reduces shear and volumetric locking but can excite zero-energy hourglass modes. Hourglass stabilization methods Automatic, Energy sampling, Hessian, Flanagan-Belytschko (explicit dynamics only), Manual or None counteract these modes. Reduced integration is always used in the explicit dynamics interfaces.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material (or other material) > Quadrature Settings > Reduced integration + Hourglass stabilization. Java parameters: reducedIntegration, hourglassStabilization, fstb, energySamplingPotential, inelasticDeformation.

parameters.name: reducedIntegration
parameters.description: 0/1 flag; default off except in explicit dynamics interfaces.

parameters.name: hourglassStabilization
parameters.description: automatic, energy sampling, Hessian, Flanagan-Belytschko, manual, none (per element type, prisms separately).

parameters.name: fstb / fstbmin
parameters.description: Hourglass stiffness multiplier and its lower bound when inelastic deformation softens the stiffness.

parameters.name: energySamplingPotential
parameters.description: linearElastic or hyperelastic (neo-Hookean) potential for large deformation.

tools.notes: Use hexahedral/quadrilateral meshes to benefit most. With the Hessian method on hex meshes enable Use full integration if hourglass modes remain. Theory: Reduced Integration and Hourglass Stabilization.

tools.name: Nonlinear Elastic Material (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Material node for stress-strain laws that are nonlinear even at small strains but path independent (no permanent set unless plasticity is added). With the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module: Ramberg-Osgood, Power law, Uniaxial data, Shear data, Bilinear elastic (different bulk modulus in tension and compression) and User defined. With the Geomechanics Module: Ramberg-Osgood, Hyperbolic law, Hardin-Drnevich, Duncan-Chang, Duncan-Selig, Small-strain overlay and User defined.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Material Models > Nonlinear Elastic Material (also Membrane). Java: physics("solid").create("nlemm1", "NonlinearElasticMaterial", 3); feature("nlemm1").set("NonlinearElasticModel", "SmallStrainOverlay"); material group NonlinearElasticMaterial (sigRef, eRef, gammaRef, n_stress, n_strain, Kt, Kc, q_ult, e_ult, sax, tau, G0).

parameters.name: Ramberg-Osgood
parameters.description: E, nu, reference stress sigma_ref, reference strain eps_ref and stress exponent n.

parameters.name: Uniaxial data / Shear data
parameters.description: Stress function of solid.eax (uniaxial strain) or solid.esh (shear strain) plus K or nu; optional nonsymmetric tension-compression curve.

parameters.name: Bilinear elastic
parameters.description: Bulk modulus in tension Kt, in compression Kc and shear modulus G (e.g. masonry, cracked media).

parameters.name: Duncan-Chang / Duncan-Selig
parameters.description: Ultimate deviatoric stress q_ult (and ultimate strain e_ult) for soils.

parameters.name: Small-strain overlay
parameters.description: Initial shear modulus G0 and reference shear strain gamma_ref with automatic or user-defined load reversal points (hysteretic soil stiffness).

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module or the Geomechanics Module. Plasticity, Creep, Viscoelasticity, Soil Plasticity etc. can be added as subnodes. User defined takes the pressure as a function of solid.eelvol plus a shear modulus.

tools.name: Neo-Hookean (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: The simplest rubber-like hyperelastic model, with strain energy depending on the first invariant of the (isochoric) elastic right Cauchy-Green tensor and the Lame parameters. It fits moderate strains well (up to roughly 20-50 % in tension) and is the default choice when only a shear modulus is known. Available as Compressible coupled (Simo-Pister or Miehe volumetric energy), Compressible uncoupled, Nearly incompressible or Incompressible.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Material model = Neo-Hookean. Java: physics("solid").create("hmm1", "HyperelasticModel", 3); feature("hmm1").set("MaterialModel", "NeoHookean"); feature("hmm1").set("Compressibility_NeoHookean", "Compressible" | "NearlyIncompressible" | "Incompressible").

parameters.name: IsotropicOption
parameters.description: Elastic pair used for the Lame parameters: Enu, EG, KG, Lame or CpCs.

parameters.name: Compressibility_NeoHookean
parameters.description: Compressible (coupled), CompressibleUncoupled, NearlyIncompressible, Incompressible.

parameters.name: VolumetricEnergyUncoupled
parameters.description: Quadratic, Polynomial, Logarithmic, Hartmann-Neff, Miehe, Simo-Taylor or user defined volumetric energy.

parameters.name: kappa
parameters.description: Bulk modulus for the nearly incompressible version (default 100 times the equivalent shear modulus).

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module (a few models are also in the MEMS/Structural Mechanics Modules). All studies become geometrically nonlinear. Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Hyperelasticity/balloon_inflation.

tools.name: Saint-Venant-Kirchhoff (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Extension of Hooke's law to large rotations: the strain energy is quadratic in the Green-Lagrange strain invariants with Lame parameters lambda and mu. It is appropriate for large displacements with small strains (slender structures, metals below yield) but becomes unstable in large compression. Compressible coupled, Compressible uncoupled and Nearly incompressible versions exist.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Material model = Saint-Venant-Kirchhoff. Java: feature("hmm1").set("MaterialModel", "SaintVenantKirchhoff"); feature("hmm1").set("Compressibility_SaintVenantKirchhoff", "Compressible").

parameters.name: Lame parameters or other elastic pair
parameters.description: Entered through IsotropicOption exactly as for Neo-Hookean.

parameters.name: Compressibility_SaintVenantKirchhoff
parameters.description: Compressible, CompressibleUncoupled or NearlyIncompressible.

tools.notes: For large-strain behavior of elastomers prefer Neo-Hookean, Mooney-Rivlin or Ogden; SVK has a non-physical softening under strong compression.

tools.name: Mooney-Rivlin (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Polynomial (Rivlin) strain energy in the first and second isochoric invariants, available with two (C10, C01), five (C10, C01, C20, C02, C11) or nine parameters (adding C30, C03, C21, C12). The two-parameter form is the classic model for rubber up to about 100 % strain; the higher-order forms capture the upturn at large stretch. The infinitesimal shear modulus is mu = 2(C10 + C01).
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Material model = Mooney-Rivlin, Two/Five/Nine Parameters. Java: feature("hmm1").set("MaterialModel", "MooneyRivlin"); feature("hmm1").set("Compressibility_MooneyRivlin", "NearlyIncompressible"); material property group MooneyRivlin with C10, C01, C11, C20, C02, C21, C12, C30, C03.

parameters.name: C10, C01 (, C20, C02, C11, C30, C03, C21, C12)
parameters.description: Model parameters (Pa), From material by default.

parameters.name: Compressibility_MooneyRivlin
parameters.description: CompressibleUncoupled, NearlyIncompressible or Incompressible.

parameters.name: Bulk modulus K / kappa
parameters.description: Volumetric stiffness for the compressible or nearly incompressible versions.

tools.notes: Parameters are usually fitted to uniaxial, biaxial and planar tension data; see Application Library Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Hyperelasticity/parameter_estimation_hyperelasticity and polynomial_hyperelastic. Negative constants can make the model unstable outside the fitted range.

tools.name: Yeoh (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Three-term polynomial in the first isochoric invariant (c1, c2, c3), developed for carbon-black filled rubbers where Neo-Hookean and Mooney-Rivlin cannot reproduce the stiffening at large strain. It fits well from uniaxial data alone because it ignores the second invariant. Used for tires, seals and boots.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Material model = Yeoh. Java: feature("hmm1").set("MaterialModel", "Yeoh"); feature("hmm1").set("Compressibility_Yeoh", "NearlyIncompressible"); material group Yeoh with c1YE, c2YE, c3YE.

parameters.name: c1YE, c2YE, c3YE
parameters.description: Yeoh model parameters c1, c2, c3 (Pa).

parameters.name: Compressibility_Yeoh
parameters.description: CompressibleUncoupled, NearlyIncompressible or Incompressible.

tools.notes: Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Hyperelasticity/rubber_boot_seal and tire_inflation.

tools.name: Ogden (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Principal-stretch based strain energy W = sum_p mu_p/alpha_p (lambda1^alpha_p + lambda2^alpha_p + lambda3^alpha_p - 3), able to fit rubber over very large strain ranges and different deformation modes. Parameters are entered as a table of (shear modulus, alpha) pairs; N = 2 or 3 terms is typical. The infinitesimal shear modulus is half the sum of mu_p*alpha_p.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Material model = Ogden, fill the Ogden parameters table. Java: feature("hmm1").set("MaterialModel", "Ogden"); feature("hmm1").set("Compressibility_Ogden", "NearlyIncompressible").

parameters.name: Ogden parameters table
parameters.description: Rows of Shear modulus mu_p (Pa) and Alpha parameter alpha_p.

parameters.name: Compressibility_Ogden
parameters.description: CompressibleUncoupled, NearlyIncompressible or Incompressible.

tools.notes: Fitting with N > 2 is difficult; check Drucker stability of the fitted set. Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Hyperelasticity/balloon_inflation (compares Neo-Hookean, Mooney-Rivlin, Ogden, Varga).

tools.name: Arruda-Boyce (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Eight-chain statistical-mechanics model with a macroscopic shear modulus mu0 and number of chain segments N that limits the chain extensibility (locking stretch sqrt(N)). The Isochoric strain energy can be the Five terms expansion or the exact Inverse Langevin function. It predicts multiaxial behavior well from uniaxial data and is also used as the spring in polymer viscoplasticity networks.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Material model = Arruda-Boyce. Java: feature("hmm1").set("MaterialModel", "ArrudaBoyce"); material group ArrudaBoyce with mu0, Nseg.

parameters.name: mu0
parameters.description: Macroscopic shear modulus (Pa).

parameters.name: Nseg
parameters.description: Number of segments N (dimensionless); smaller N means earlier stiffening.

parameters.name: Isochoric strain energy
parameters.description: Five terms expansion or Inverse Langevin function (HyperelasticEnergy5termsInvLangevin).

tools.notes: Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Viscoplasticity/chloroprene_rubber_compression_test (Arruda-Boyce with Bergstrom-Boyce network).

tools.name: Gent (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Limited-extensibility model W = -(mu*jm/2) ln(1 - (I1-3)/jm) with shear modulus mu and parameter jm, the maximum value of I1-3. It reproduces the sharp stiffening of rubber and biological tissue near the chain-locking limit with only two parameters and reduces to Neo-Hookean for jm to infinity.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Material model = Gent. Java: the compressibility key is Compressibility_Gent (e.g. "NearlyIncompressible"); the MaterialModel value follows the same naming pattern.

parameters.name: Macroscopic shear modulus mu
parameters.description: Initial shear modulus (Pa), From material.

parameters.name: jm
parameters.description: Limiting value of I1 - 3 (dimensionless).

parameters.name: Compressibility_Gent
parameters.description: Compressible uncoupled, nearly incompressible or incompressible.

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material 1 > Material model: Gent
Compressibility: Nearly incompressible
Macroscopic shear modulus mu = 0.4[MPa], jm = 80
model.component("comp1").physics("solid").feature("hmm1").set("Compressibility_Gent", "NearlyIncompressible");
tools.notes: Also offered as spring model in the Parallel Network option of Polymer Viscoplasticity.

tools.name: Storakers (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Ogden-type model for highly compressible elastomeric foams in which each term has a shear modulus, an alpha exponent and a beta parameter controlling compressibility (effective Poisson's ratio). It is used for crushable foams, cushioning and packaging materials that undergo large volumetric deformation.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Material model = Storakers, fill the Storakers parameters table (Shear modulus, Alpha parameter, Beta parameter).

parameters.name: Storakers parameters table
parameters.description: Rows of mu_p (Pa), alpha_p and beta_p.

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material 1 > Material model: Storakers
Table row 1: Shear modulus 0.2[MPa], Alpha 8, Beta 0.1
(beta relates to an effective Poisson's ratio nu = beta/(1+2*beta))
tools.notes: Always compressible; do not use a mixed incompressible formulation. For permanent foam crushing use Pressure-Dependent Plasticity (Foam) instead.

tools.name: Varga (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Stretch-based model linear in the sum of principal stretches (c1) with an optional second-order term (c2); it gives a good fit to natural rubber at moderate strains and is numerically robust. It is compared against other models in the balloon inflation benchmark.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Material model = Varga. Java: feature("hmm1").set("MaterialModel", "Varga"); material group Varga with c1VA, c2VA.

parameters.name: c1VA, c2VA
parameters.description: Varga model parameters c1 and c2 (Pa).

parameters.name: Compressibility_Varga
parameters.description: Compressible uncoupled, nearly incompressible or incompressible.

tools.notes: Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Hyperelasticity/balloon_inflation.

tools.name: Murnaghan (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Third-order elasticity model using the Lame parameters plus Murnaghan constants l, m and n. It describes the small change of stiffness with prestress and is used for acoustoelasticity: stress-dependent wave speeds, ultrasonic stress measurement and residual stress in rails.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Material model = Murnaghan. Material property group Murnaghan with l, m, n plus the Lame group.

parameters.name: l, m, n
parameters.description: Murnaghan third-order elastic moduli (Pa).

parameters.name: lambda, mu
parameters.description: Second-order Lame parameters.

tools.notes: Typically combined with a prestressed Eigenfrequency or Frequency Domain study. Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Hyperelasticity/rail_steel.

tools.name: Blatz-Ko, Gao and van der Waals (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Additional predefined strain energy models: Blatz-Ko (shear modulus mu with parameters beta and phi) for compressible polyurethane foams; Gao (parameters a and n) for materials with a power-law stiffening response; and van der Waals (shear modulus, maximum chain stretch lambda_m, chain network interaction alpha and weight beta), a statistical network model that includes attractive chain interaction.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Material model = Blatz-Ko | Gao | van der Waals. Java: Compressibility_vanDerWaals is the compressibility parameter for the van der Waals model.

parameters.name: Blatz-Ko: mu, beta, phi
parameters.description: Shear modulus and model parameters.

parameters.name: Gao: a, n
parameters.description: Model parameters.

parameters.name: van der Waals: mu, lambda_m, alpha, beta
parameters.description: Shear modulus, locking stretch, interaction parameter and weight between I1 and I2.

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material 1 > Material model: van der Waals
Shear modulus 0.5[MPa], Maximum chain stretch 10, Chain network interaction 0.2, Weight 0
tools.notes: Blatz-Ko is compressible by construction; choose it for foams with an effective Poisson's ratio near 0.25.

tools.name: Delfino, Fung and Extended Tube (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Models aimed at soft biological tissue and filled rubber: Delfino (exponential in I1, parameters a and b) for arterial walls; Fung (exponential of a quadratic form of the Green-Lagrange strain with an anisotropic coefficient matrix A and parameter c) for anisotropic soft tissue; and Extended Tube (Gc, Ge, alpha, beta) based on tube-model polymer physics with finite extensibility. Fiber families are added with the Fiber subnode (for example Holzapfel-Gasser-Ogden).
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Material model = Delfino | Fung | Extended Tube. Java compressibility keys: Compressibility_Delfino, Compressibility_Fung, Compressibility_ExtendedTube.

parameters.name: Delfino: a, b
parameters.description: Stress-like and exponential parameters.

parameters.name: Fung: A (6x6), c
parameters.description: Coefficient matrix in the local coordinate system (Standard or Voigt) and scale parameter c.

parameters.name: Extended Tube: Gc, Ge, alpha, beta
parameters.description: Crosslink and entanglement moduli, extensibility and empirical exponent.

tools.notes: Fung compressibility is Compressible by default in the Application Library models. For fibre-reinforced tissue combine a matrix model with Fiber (HGO).

tools.name: User-Defined Strain Energy Density (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Enter your own hyperelastic law as an expression of the invariants or components of the elastic right Cauchy-Green tensor (or of the elastic deformation gradient). Compressible materials take a total energy Ws; Nearly incompressible materials take an isochoric energy Wsiso plus volumetric energy Wvol; Incompressible adds a Lagrange multiplier. COMSOL differentiates the expression symbolically to obtain stresses and tangents.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Material model = User defined. Java: feature("hmm1").set("MaterialModel", "userDefined"); feature("hmm1").set("Compressibility_UserDef", "NearlyIncompressible"); feature("hmm1").set("Wsiso", "<expression>").

parameters.name: Ws / Wsiso / Wvol
parameters.description: Strain energy densities written with solid.I1CIel, solid.I2CIel, solid.Jel, solid.CIel11 etc.

parameters.name: Use elastic deformation gradient
parameters.description: Write the energy in terms of Fel components instead of Cel.

parameters.name: Equivalent Young's/shear modulus (Advanced)
parameters.description: Eeq, Geq used for contact penalty factors and stabilization; defaults 1 GPa and Eeq/3.

tools.notes: Not available in Solid Mechanics, Explicit Dynamics. Always set realistic equivalent moduli under Advanced, otherwise contact penalties may be badly scaled.

tools.name: Compressibility and Volumetric Strain Energy (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Each hyperelastic model offers Compressible coupled, Compressible uncoupled, Nearly incompressible and/or Incompressible variants. Uncoupled forms split W into isochoric and volumetric parts, and the volumetric energy can be Quadratic, Polynomial (K, K2, K3), Logarithmic, Hartmann-Neff, Miehe, Simo-Taylor or user defined. Nearly incompressible adds an auxiliary pressure (perturbed Lagrangian); Incompressible enforces Jel = 1 with a Lagrange multiplier.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > Compressibility list and Volumetric strain energy density list. Java: Compressibility_<Model> and VolumetricEnergyUncoupled (quadratic, hartmannNeff, miehe, userDefined, ...).

parameters.name: Compressibility_<Model>
parameters.description: Compressible, CompressibleUncoupled, NearlyIncompressible or Incompressible (options depend on the model).

parameters.name: VolumetricEnergyUncoupled
parameters.description: quadratic (only option giving a symmetric mixed stiffness matrix), polynomial, logarithmic, hartmannNeff, miehe, simoTaylor, userDefined.

parameters.name: kappa
parameters.description: Bulk modulus; default 100 x shear modulus, about nu = 0.495.

tools.notes: Fully incompressible formulations are not available in plane stress with some options and in explicit dynamics (Compressible coupled/uncoupled only).

tools.name: Mullins Effect (Hyperelastic Material)
tools.description: Subnode to Hyperelastic Material that models the stress softening of filled elastomers after the first load cycle (damage depending on the maximum strain energy reached). The damage function is Ogden-Roxburgh (maximum damage, damage saturation energy, deformation dependence coefficient, optional error function) or Miehe.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material > (right-click) Mullins Effect; also Shell > Hyperelastic Material, Layered, Layered Shell and Membrane.

parameters.name: Damage function
parameters.description: Ogden-Roxburgh or Miehe.

parameters.name: d_inf
parameters.description: Maximum damage (default 1).

parameters.name: W_sat
parameters.description: Damage saturation strain energy (default 1 MJ/m^3).

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: Deformation dependence coefficient (Ogden-Roxburgh, default 0).

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material 1 (Yeoh) > Mullins Effect 1
Damage function: Ogden-Roxburgh, d_inf = 0.4, W_sat = 0.5[MJ/m^3]
Study: Time Dependent or Stationary with an auxiliary sweep of a load-unload-reload cycle
tools.notes: Only affects the response under cyclic or non-monotonic loading; combine with Viscoelasticity for rate effects.

tools.name: Fiber (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Adds one or more families of stiff fibers in given directions to a Linear Elastic, Nonlinear Elastic or Hyperelastic matrix, assuming a small fiber volume. For linear/nonlinear matrices the fiber is Linear elastic or Uniaxial data; for hyperelastic matrices the options are Holzapfel-Gasser-Ogden (k1, k2, dispersion k3), Linear elastic, Uniaxial data or User defined energy. Typical uses are arterial walls, myocardium, tire cords and reinforced polymers.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic / Hyperelastic Material > Fiber. Java: feature("hmm1").create("fib1", "Fiber", 3); feature("hmm1").feature("fib1").set("HyperModelSelection", "HolzapfelGasserOgden"); material group HolzapfelGasserOgden with k1HGO, k2HGO, k3HGO. Edge fibers in thin layers use type FiberTL.

parameters.name: HyperModelSelection
parameters.description: HolzapfelGasserOgden, linear elastic, uniaxial data or user defined (hyperelastic matrix).

parameters.name: directionSelection / direction
parameters.description: Fiber direction as a local axis (x1, x2, x3) of the chosen coordinate system or a user-defined vector.

parameters.name: tensileStiffOnly
parameters.description: Fibers contribute only in tension.

parameters.name: contributeToTotalStress
parameters.description: Add fiber stress to the matrix stress tensor (usually off).

parameters.name: Fiber_material
parameters.description: Domain material or a separate Material node that holds the fiber properties.

tools.notes: Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Hyperelasticity/biventricular_cardiac_model and tire_inflation (FiberTL in thin layers). Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module.

tools.name: Generalized Maxwell (Viscoelasticity)
tools.description: Default linear viscoelastic model: a long-term spring (the parent material) in parallel with any number of spring-dashpot branches, each with shear (and/or bulk) modulus and relaxation time, i.e. a Prony series. It can be used in time-dependent, frequency-domain and eigenfrequency studies; branches can be pruned to a frequency band and fractional derivatives can replace the dashpots. For hyperelastic parents each branch has an energy factor instead of moduli (large strain viscoelasticity).
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material (or Hyperelastic/Nonlinear Elastic) > Viscoelasticity > Material model = Generalized Maxwell. Java: feature("lemm1").create("vis1", "Viscoelasticity", 3); feature("lemm1").feature("vis1").set("MaterialModel", "GeneralizedMaxwell").

parameters.name: Branch table
parameters.description: Bulk modulus Km and/or shear modulus Gm with relaxation time tau_m per branch (energy factor beta_vm for large strain).

parameters.name: deformationModel
parameters.description: Viscoelastic strains: deviatoric (default), volumetric, or full (volumetric and deviatoric).

parameters.name: StaticResponse
parameters.description: Stiffness used in stationary studies: LongTerm or Instantaneous.

parameters.name: pruneBranches, f_lower, f_upper
parameters.description: Remove branches outside a frequency band to reduce the number of variables.

parameters.name: UseFractDeriv
parameters.description: Replace dashpots by spring-pots of fractional order beta_m.

tools.notes: Branch data can be loaded from a text file. Application Library: Structural_Mechanics_Module/Dynamics_and_Vibration/viscoelastic_damper_transient, _frequency and _eigenmodes. Requires the Structural Mechanics or Nonlinear Structural Materials Module (large strain needs NSM).

tools.name: Kelvin-Voigt and Generalized Kelvin-Voigt (Viscoelasticity)
tools.description: Kelvin-Voigt places a single dashpot in parallel with the parent spring (creeping solid, no instantaneous elastic jump), defined by a relaxation time or viscosity. Generalized Kelvin-Voigt chains several spring-dashpot Kelvin elements in series with the parent spring and suits retardation (creep compliance) data. Both can use fractional derivatives.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Viscoelasticity > Material model = Kelvin-Voigt or Generalized Kelvin-Voigt.

parameters.name: Relaxation data
parameters.description: Relaxation time tau_v (default 1 ms) or viscosity eta_v (default 1000 Pa s).

parameters.name: Branch table (generalized)
parameters.description: Km/Gm and tau_m for each Kelvin element in series.

parameters.name: Use fractional derivatives
parameters.description: Fractional order beta_v of the spring-pot (default 0.8).

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material 1 > Viscoelasticity 1
Material model: Kelvin-Voigt, Viscoelastic strains: Deviatoric
Relaxation data: Viscosity, eta_v = 5e4[Pa*s]
tools.notes: The instantaneous stiffness equals the parent material stiffness; with Generalized Kelvin-Voigt the long-term compliance is the sum of the element compliances.

tools.name: Standard Linear Solid and Maxwell (Viscoelasticity)
tools.description: Standard linear solid (Zener) adds one spring-dashpot branch (Kv, Gv and relaxation time or viscosity) in parallel with the long-term parent spring; for large strains an energy factor is used. Maxwell uses a single dashpot in series with the parent spring, so the material relaxes to zero stress (fluid-like). With fractional derivatives, an approximation to a Generalized Maxwell series can be computed for time-domain and eigenfrequency use.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Viscoelasticity > Material model = Standard linear solid or Maxwell. Java parameter keys: Kv, Gv, tauv, etav, RelaxationParameter (RelaxationTime/Viscosity), betav (energy factor).

parameters.name: Kv, Gv
parameters.description: Branch bulk and shear modulus (defaults 10 MPa and 1 MPa).

parameters.name: tauv / etav
parameters.description: Relaxation time (1 ms) or dashpot viscosity (1000 Pa s).

parameters.name: betav
parameters.description: Energy factor of the branch for large-strain viscoelasticity (default 0.2).

parameters.name: Compute approximation
parameters.description: Preprocessing action for fractional models so they can run in Time Dependent/Eigenfrequency studies.

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material 1 > Viscoelasticity 1
Material model: Standard linear solid, Viscoelastic strains: Deviatoric
Energy factor beta_v = 0.2, Relaxation time tau_v = 1[ms]
// Java keys seen in library models: set("betav", "0.2"), set("tauv", "1[ms]")
tools.notes: Several Viscoelasticity subnodes under one parent are additive. Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Viscoelasticity/golf_ball_impact (large-strain viscoelastic hyperelastic ball). The MaterialModel string for this option was not present in the local library models, so read it from GUI-generated code (File > Save As Java).

tools.name: Burgers (Viscoelasticity)
tools.description: Four-parameter rheology combining a Maxwell element with a Kelvin-Voigt element in series (parent spring + dashpot + spring-dashpot pair). It captures instantaneous elasticity, delayed elasticity and unbounded viscous flow, and is common for asphalt, ice, rock salt and polymer creep.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Viscoelasticity > Material model = Burgers.

parameters.name: Kv2, Gv2
parameters.description: Bulk/shear modulus of the second (Kelvin) spring, default 1 MPa.

parameters.name: tau_v1, tau_v2 or eta_v1, eta_v2
parameters.description: Relaxation times (1 ms, 10 ms) or viscosities (1000 and 100 Pa s) of the two dashpots.

parameters.name: beta_v1, beta_v2
parameters.description: Fractional orders when fractional derivatives are enabled (0.8, 0.9).

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material 1 > Viscoelasticity 1
Material model: Burgers, Viscoelastic strains: Deviatoric
G_v2 = 50[MPa], eta_v1 = 1e12[Pa*s], eta_v2 = 1e10[Pa*s]
Study: Time Dependent over hours with a sustained load
tools.notes: Like Maxwell, a Burgers solid has no long-term stiffness from the dashpot branch; ensure proper supports in stationary studies (Instantaneous stiffness).

tools.name: User-Defined Storage and Loss Moduli (Viscoelasticity)
tools.description: Frequency-domain viscoelasticity given directly as storage and loss moduli (K', K'', G', G''), storage and loss compliances, or a loss factor, typically as interpolation functions of the frequency variable solid.freq from DMA measurements. An approximation by a Generalized Maxwell series can be computed so that the same data are usable in Eigenfrequency and Time Dependent studies.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Viscoelasticity > Material model = User defined. Java: feature("vis1").set("MaterialModel", "userDef"); set("userDefInput", "moduli"); set("Gstor", "gstor(solid.freq)"); set("Gloss", "gloss(solid.freq)").

parameters.name: userDefInput
parameters.description: moduli (storage/loss moduli), compliances or loss factor.

parameters.name: Kstor/Kloss, Gstor/Gloss
parameters.description: Frequency-dependent volumetric and deviatoric storage and loss moduli.

parameters.name: Time Domain and Eigenfrequency: Compute approximation
parameters.description: Fits a Maxwell series to the data; preview and inspect the fitted parameters.

tools.notes: Without the approximation, the user-defined model is valid only in Frequency Domain; eigenvalue problems become nonlinear. Application Library: Structural_Mechanics_Module/Dynamics_and_Vibration/viscoelastic_damper_frequency.

tools.name: Shift Functions WLF, Arrhenius and TNM (Viscoelasticity)
tools.description: Thermal Effects section of the Viscoelasticity node for thermorheologically simple materials: relaxation times are scaled by a shift factor aT(T). Options are None, Williams-Landel-Ferry (Tref, C1, C2), Arrhenius (Tref, activation energy Q), Tool-Narayanaswamy-Moynihan (Tref, Q, activation energy fraction chi, structural relaxation time lambda0, for glass) and User defined.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Viscoelasticity > Thermal Effects > Shift function. Java: set("shiftFunction", "shiftWLF"); set("Twlf", "293.15[K]"); set("C1wlf", "17.44"); set("C2wlf", "51.6[K]").

parameters.name: shiftFunction
parameters.description: none, shiftWLF, Arrhenius, Tool-Narayanaswamy-Moynihan, user defined.

parameters.name: Twlf, C1wlf, C2wlf
parameters.description: WLF reference temperature and constants (defaults 293.15 K, 17.44, 51.6 K).

parameters.name: T0, Q
parameters.description: Reference temperature and activation energy for Arrhenius/TNM.

parameters.name: chi, lambda0
parameters.description: TNM activation energy fraction and structural relaxation time.

tools.notes: The temperature comes from the Model Input (e.g. a Heat Transfer interface). TNM is typically used for glass tempering and annealing simulations.

tools.name: Rayleigh Damping (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Damping proportional to mass and stiffness, C = alpha_dM*M + beta_dK*K, usable in Eigenfrequency, Frequency Domain and Time Dependent studies. Parameters can be given directly (Alpha and beta) or derived from damping ratios zeta1, zeta2 at two frequencies f1, f2, with a Damping Ratio Preview plot. It is the usual choice for transient structural dynamics when only modal damping ratios are known.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Damping > Damping type = Rayleigh damping. Java: feature("lemm1").create("dmp1", "Damping", 3); feature("lemm1").feature("dmp1").set("DampingType", "RayleighDamping"); set("InputParameters", "AlphaBeta" | "DampingRatios").

parameters.name: alpha_dM, beta_dK
parameters.description: Mass (1/s) and stiffness (s) damping parameters.

parameters.name: f1, zeta1, f2, zeta2
parameters.description: Two frequency/damping-ratio pairs when InputParameters = DampingRatios.

tools.notes: Rayleigh damping in the Beam interface is ignored for geometrically nonlinear analysis. Mass damping over-damps low-frequency rigid-body-like motion. See Damping (structural) for the general node.

tools.name: Loss Factor Damping (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Hysteretic (structural) damping represented by complex-valued stiffness D(1 + i*eta). Isotropic loss factor uses one eta_s applied to all elastic constants; Anisotropic loss factor uses a symmetric 6x6 loss-factor matrix eta_D. Maximum loss factor gives an approximately frequency-independent loss over a band that also works in time domain. Loss factor damping is effective only in Eigenfrequency and Frequency Domain studies.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Damping > Damping type = Isotropic loss factor | Anisotropic loss factor | Maximum loss factor. Java: set("DampingType", "IsotropicLossFactor"); set("eta_s_mat", "userdef"); set("eta_s", "0.02").

parameters.name: eta_s
parameters.description: Isotropic structural loss factor (From material or User defined).

parameters.name: eta_D / eta_DVo
parameters.description: Anisotropic loss factor matrix in the parent node's coordinate system.

parameters.name: eta_max, f_ref
parameters.description: Maximum loss factor and its frequency for the Maximum loss factor option.

tools.notes: Equivalence: at resonance, eta = 2*zeta. Loss factor makes eigenfrequencies complex; the quality factor Q = 1/eta. Ignored in time-dependent studies (use Rayleigh or Maximum loss factor there).

tools.name: Viscous Damping and Wave Attenuation (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Viscous damping adds a stress proportional to the strain rate through bulk viscosity eta_b and shear viscosity eta_v, giving damping that grows with frequency; it works in time and frequency domain. Wave attenuation defines damping from measured attenuation of pressure and shear waves (Np/m, dB/m, dB per wavelength) at reference frequencies, convenient for ultrasonics and geophysics.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Damping > Damping type = Viscous damping or Wave attenuation. Java: set("DampingType", "ViscousDamping"); set("etab", ...); set("etav", ...); attenuation keys alphap_dBm, alphas_dBm, AttenuationUnit.

parameters.name: etab, etav
parameters.description: Bulk and shear viscosity (Pa s).

parameters.name: AttenuationUnit
parameters.description: Np/m, dB/m, dB/lambda, etc. for Wave attenuation.

parameters.name: alphap_*, alphas_*, fp_ref, fs_ref
parameters.description: P- and S-wave attenuation and reference frequencies.

tools.notes: See Equivalence Between Loss Factor, Rayleigh, and Viscous Damping in the user's guide to convert between models.

tools.name: Lagoudas (Shape Memory Alloy)
tools.description: Shape Memory Alloy material with the Lagoudas model for superelasticity and the shape memory effect in NiTi and similar alloys. Separate austenite and martensite materials supply Young's moduli and heat capacities; the phase diagram is given by martensite/austenite start and finish temperatures (or stresses) and the slopes CM and CA; the transformation kinetics can be Quadratic, Cosine, Smooth or User defined, with constant or exponential maximum transformation strain.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Material Models > Shape Memory Alloy, Shape memory alloy model = Lagoudas. Java: physics("solid").create("sma1", "ShapeMemoryAlloy", 3); feature("sma1").set("ShapeMemoryAlloyModel", "Lagoudas"); material groups ShapeMemoryAlloyAustenite (E_A, Cp_A), ShapeMemoryAlloyMartensite (E_M, Cp_M), LagoudasModel (T0, TMs, TMf, TAs, TAf, CM, CA, etrmaxLagoudas, sigmaStar).

parameters.name: AusteniteMaterial / MartensiteMaterial
parameters.description: Material nodes holding the phase properties.

parameters.name: TransformationParameters
parameters.description: Temperature (Ms, Mf, As, Af, CM, CA) or Stress (sigma_Ms, sigma_Mf, sigma_As, sigma_Af at T_sigma).

parameters.name: MaximumTransformationStrain
parameters.description: Constant (etr_max) or Exponential law.

parameters.name: TransformationFunction
parameters.description: Quadratic, Cosine, Smooth (eta1..eta4) or User defined.

parameters.name: Phase Transformation Direction subnode
parameters.description: Automatic or User defined transformation direction.

tools.notes: Requires the Nonlinear Structural Materials Module. Result templates: Martensite Volume Fraction and SMA phase diagram. Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Shape_Memory_Alloys/sma_stent and uniaxial_loading_of_shape_memory_alloy.

tools.name: Souza-Auricchio (Shape Memory Alloy)
tools.description: Alternative SMA model with a single transformation strain tensor as internal variable, well suited for 3D multiaxial and non-proportional loading and large-scale structures such as stents. The equivalent stress is von Mises or Prager-Lode (tension-compression asymmetry through a stress ratio); phase transition data are given in Standard (elastic domain radius, hardening modulus, reference temperature), Stress or Temperature form.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Shape Memory Alloy > Shape memory alloy model = Souza-Auricchio. Java: feature("sma1").set("ShapeMemoryAlloyModel", "SouzaAuricchio"); set("TransformationParametersAuricchio", "standard" | "temperature"); material group SouzaAuricchioModel (TStar, beta, etrmaxAuricchio, sig0_SA, Hk, ...).

parameters.name: equivalentStressAuricchio
parameters.description: mises or Prager-Lode with stressRatio (compression/tension elastic radius).

parameters.name: beta, etrmaxAuricchio
parameters.description: Slope of the limit curve and maximum transformation strain.

parameters.name: sig0_SA, Hk, TStar
parameters.description: Elastic domain radius, hardening modulus, reference temperature (Standard input).

tools.notes: Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Shape_Memory_Alloys/uniaxial_loading_of_shape_memory_alloy_souza_auricchio.

tools.name: Piezomagnetic Material (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Linear magnetoelastic material for linearized magnetostriction, entered in strain-magnetization form (compliance sH, coupling dHT, permeability muT) or stress-magnetization form (elasticity cH, coupling eHS, muS) in Voigt order. It is added automatically by the Piezomagnetism multiphysics interface together with an Ampere's Law, Piezomagnetic node; without an active coupling it acts as a plain elastic material.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Material Models > Piezomagnetic Material (normally created by Add Multiphysics > Piezomagnetism).

parameters.name: Constitutive relation
parameters.description: Strain-magnetization form or Stress-magnetization form.

parameters.name: sH / cH
parameters.description: Compliance or elasticity matrix at constant magnetic field (Voigt).

parameters.name: dHT / eHS
parameters.description: Piezomagnetic coupling matrix.

parameters.name: Use multiplicative formulation
parameters.description: Multiplicative decomposition of elastic and piezomagnetic strains for large deformation.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics or MEMS Module with the AC/DC Module. The older Magnetostrictive Material node is obsolete since 6.1; use Piezomagnetism (linear) or Nonlinear Magnetostriction instead.

tools.name: External Stress-Strain Relation (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Material node that delegates the stress computation to compiled user code (a shared library, e.g. UMAT-style C code) imported as an External Material under Global Definitions > Materials. The library receives strains or the deformation gradient (Green-Lagrange/second Piola-Kirchhoff in total Lagrangian kinematics) plus model inputs and returns stresses, tangents and state variables.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Materials > External Material (import .dll/.so), then Solid Mechanics > Material Models > External Stress-Strain Relation > Material = the external material.

parameters.name: External material
parameters.description: Compatible External Material whose Interface type matches the inputs this node provides.

parameters.name: Geometric Nonlinearity
parameters.description: Formulation and strain decomposition as for other material models.

tools.example:
Global Definitions > Materials > External Material 1: Library = myumat.dll, Interface type = General stress-strain relation
Solid Mechanics > External Stress-Strain Relation 1: Material = External Material 1
Study: Stationary with geometric nonlinearity
tools.notes: See the existing entry External Material (user-defined material models in C). States are stored per Gauss point; ensure consistent tangent for Newton convergence.

tools.name: Inelastic Strain Rate (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Adds an inelastic contribution given as a rate (strain tensor rate, deformation gradient rate, its inverse or stretches) that COMSOL integrates in time, as opposed to External Strain which prescribes the strain itself. It is a flexible way to implement custom creep, swelling or growth laws without writing a full material model.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic / Nonlinear Elastic / Hyperelastic Material > Inelastic Strain Rate.

parameters.name: Strain input
parameters.description: Strain tensor, Deformation gradient, Deformation gradient inverse or Stretches (strain tensor not for hyperelastic).

parameters.name: Initial value
parameters.description: Initial inelastic quantity.

parameters.name: Time stepping method
parameters.description: Automatic, Backward Euler (local Newton tolerances) or Domain ODEs.

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material 1 > Inelastic Strain Rate 1
Strain input: Strain tensor, rate components e.g. A*(solid.mises/1[MPa])^n*solid.sx/solid.mises (custom creep law)
Study: Time Dependent
tools.notes: Available in Solid Mechanics, Shell (layered), Layered Shell and Membrane; layered formulations always use domain ODEs.

tools.name: Intercalation Strain (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Volumetric strain caused by insertion of species into a host lattice, e.g. lithium intercalation in battery electrode particles; the strain is dV(c)/3 times identity for small strain or a deformation gradient for large strain. The volumetric strain function comes from the electrode material or a user expression of the concentration.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic / Nonlinear Elastic / Hyperelastic Material > Intercalation Strain. Java: feature("lemm1").create("ic1", "IntercalationStrain", 3).

parameters.name: Volumetric strain dV
parameters.description: From material (Volumetric strain property as function of concentration) or User defined.

parameters.name: dV_ref
parameters.description: Reference volumetric strain at which the intercalation strain is zero.

parameters.name: Concentration (Model Input)
parameters.description: Concentration variable, e.g. from a Lithium-Ion Battery or Transport interface.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("solid").feature("lemm1").create("ic1", "IntercalationStrain", 3);
// Volumetric strain From material (graphite electrode), concentration from liion.cs_surface
tools.notes: Requires the Battery Design Module. For generic species-induced swelling use the Shrinkage and Swelling coupling or Hygroscopic Swelling.

tools.name: Activation (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Subnode that activates or deactivates material according to a Boolean Activation expression, emulating element birth and death. Inactive material has its stiffness scaled by the activation scale factor (default 1e-5) and density by its square; at activation the previous elastic strain is removed so the new material starts stress free. Used for additive manufacturing, staged construction, excavation and curing.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Activation (also Wire > Elastic Wire and the explicit dynamics interfaces). Java: feature("lemm1").create("act1", "Activation", 2); set("activation_expression", ...); set("actfac", "1e-5").

parameters.name: activation_expression
parameters.description: Boolean expression; material is active where true (e.g. t > t_layer or Temp < T_cure).

parameters.name: actfac
parameters.description: Activation scale factor applied to stiffness when inactive (default 1e-5).

tools.notes: Initial stresses are always removed at activation; external stresses are not. Application Library: Geomechanics_Module/Soil/tunnel_excavation and Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Porous_Plasticity/two_stage_compaction.

tools.name: Safety (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Subnode that evaluates failure criteria without affecting the solution, producing failure index FI, damage index DI, safety factor SF and margin of safety MoS. Criteria for isotropic materials include von Mises, Tresca, Rankine, Saint-Venant (strain), Mohr-Coulomb (optional elliptic cap), Drucker-Prager, Griffith, Bresler-Pister, Willam-Warnke, Ottosen, Jenkins, Waddoups, plus orthotropic/anisotropic criteria (Tsai-Hill, Hoffman, Tsai-Wu) and User defined. Several Safety nodes can be added after solving and evaluated with Update Solution.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material (or Nonlinear Elastic, Linear Elastic Layered) > Safety. Java: feature("lemm1").create("sf1", "Safety", 3); feature("lemm1").feature("sf1").set("FailureCriterion", "Von Mises"); set("sigmat", "350[MPa]").

parameters.name: FailureCriterion
parameters.description: "Von Mises", "Rankine", "Tsai-Hill", "Hoffman", "Tsai-Wu Orthotropic", "Tsai-Wu Anisotropic", "User defined", etc.

parameters.name: sigmat, sigmac
parameters.description: Tensile and compressive strengths; Mohr-Coulomb uses cohesion and friction angle.

parameters.name: Result variables
parameters.description: Failure index, damage index, safety factor and margin of safety defined per Safety node (Table 4-2 of the user's guide); they appear under the node in the expression list after Update Solution.

tools.notes: For composite criteria (Hashin, Puck, LaRC03, Zinoviev) see the Composite Materials entries. Requires the Structural Mechanics Module or another add-on (see product specifications).
